title: Semaphore rollout for autonomous batching reconciler
creator: Leah Martinez
description:
Problem statement: Optimize engine suggests batching and KV cache changes that reduce per-token cost, but previous bulk auto-applies risked noisy regressions and user latency spikes. We need an enforcement layer that sequences application of Optimize suggestions through a semaphore-driven rollout (coordinator) that gates concurrent applies, orchestrates small canaries, enforces metric checks, and exposes operator approvals when thresholds are crossed.

Objective: Build a reconciler that: 1) consumes Optimize suggestions, 2) acquires a rollout semaphore to limit concurrent active applies across tenants, 3) launches canary subsets with traffic split rules, 4) monitors a defined metric vector (latency P95, error-rate, quality regression score, cost-per-inference), 5) auto-commits or rollbacks based on thresholds, and 6) surfaces approvals to Console for manual override.

High-level constraints: Must integrate with existing rollout API, support Dedicated and Hosted customers (respecting tenancy isolation), be idempotent for retries, and play well with the existing autoscaler and KV cache fast-paths.
acceptance_criteria: Semaphore coordinator limits concurrent apply jobs to configured capacity and reports active count to Console.
Canary groups (1%, 10%, 30%) can be created and torn down automatically by the reconciler using existing routing policies.
Metric watch triggers commit when cost reduction >= 12% and quality regression < 0.5 pts for 30m sustained, otherwise triggers rollback.
Operator can pause, force-commit, or force-rollback from Console with audit log entry and linked run ID.
Rollout run includes deterministic simulation artifacts (dry-run diff) available in the ticket and Console.
End-to-end test coverage for happy path, transient infra failures, and a forced rollback scenario.
No customer-visible downtime during canary progression; latency SLO violations are detected and cause immediate rollback.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Dry-run simulation mode against a sampled shard of traffic (no config mutation).
Phase 1: Acquire semaphore and apply to 1% canary for 30 minutes. Collect metrics and checksums of responses for quality eval.
Phase 2: Expand to 10% if checks pass for 60 minutes; otherwise rollback and mark suggestion noisy.
Phase 3: Expand to 30% for 2 hours with continued monitoring. If still green, notify PM for scheduled full apply or auto-commit based on policy.
Abort: Any P95 latency regression > 20% or error-rate increase > 0.5 percentage points triggers immediate rollback and circuit-open for that suggestion for 24h.
metrics_and_alerts: 5xx error rate - watch for +0.5pp absolute increase
Quality regression score (eval harness using golden prompts) - max 0.5 pts delta
Cost-per-token - expected reduction target >= 12% with 5% tolerance
Semaphore saturation metric - warn if > 80% of semaphore slots used
test_plan: Unit tests for semaphore acquisition/release, e2e integration test that spins up local fake routing and feeding harness, chaos scenarios where KV cache misses spike, and a scoring harness to assert quality delta detection. Add a nightly long-run that exercises canary expansion and rollback. Link to test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize-reconciler/tree/sem-rollout-tests
implementation_notes: Coordinator (go) service with a persistent semaphore stored in Postgres using advisory locks to support multi-region controllers.
Use existing rollout-controller API for traffic-slicing; extend with small 'canaryTemplate' to declare metric watches.
Quality scoring will call the eval microservice (eval-service) with sampled prompts; limit sample size to 1k responses per canary window to bound cost.
Designed for eventual compatibility with Private deployments: controller runs as a control-plane sidecar in VPC via RPC tunnel; auth respects KMS-scoped keys.
Include a dry-run diff generator that emits a compact JSON patch for Console to show proposed changes and expected cost delta.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: A noisy suggestion could cause multiple rollbacks and operator fatigue. Mitigation: circuit-open noisy suggestions and surface root-cause (model change vs config).
Risk: Semaphore becomes single point of contention. Mitigation: partition semaphores by tenant cohort and provide a fallback queue with exponential backoff.
Risk: Eval harness false positives (quality noise). Mitigation: use ensemble of heuristics and duplicate human-in-the-loop sample for high-impact suggestions.
Risk: Cross-region latency during control-plane actions. Mitigation: prefer local region controllers with lease-based tokens and conservative timings.
